title: Approval and landing steps in the contract, with human checks recorded at approval

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
v8 ends at "land when the owner authorizes it" and names no procedure. ork's run landed 40+ slices with one script: rerun the checks, commit, merge main into the branch when main moved (with slicer's merge drivers), `slicer render`, commit, `slicer check`, rerun the suite, ff-only merge, `relay-run end`, push when authorized, remove the worktree and branch. After a merge, goldens can need a rebaseline (ork S118 on 2026-10-26, after S110 changed the sidebar). ork decided adj 162 (`landing.in-ork`) and builds it as S119. `docs/landing.md` describes a `--no-ff` merge and `slicer land`, which differs from this flow.

Human checks (`[HUMAN CHECK]` lines in Check) have no contract step. In ork's run they piled up as adj records (141-147) for days. ork S118 shows them on the approval card and records each tick as a slicer note.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: a Land section and an Approve step in `ai relay`.
- `docs/landing.md`: the relay landing flow beside the manual one.
- `src/slicer/config.py`: a `human-check` note kind in the default `note_kinds`, if chosen.
- The contract golden fixture.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. An Approve step after the finish step: the owner sees the gate verdict, tests, diff stat, owner findings and human checks, and approves, or sends a fix note to a fix round.
2. Each human check is recorded as a note (`--kind human-check` where configured).
3. A Land step lists the order above and names `slicer land`.
Owner decisions needed: ff-only or `--no-ff` as the contract default; whether an unmarked human check blocks landing.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-26: the contract's default landing is ff-only (merge main into the branch when main moved, re-render, check, rerun the suite, then `git merge --ff-only`). An unrecorded human check is shown at approval and warns; it does not block landing.
